source.dataset: TotalSegmentator dataset v2.0.1 (Wasserthal J. et al., Radiology: Artificial Intelligence 2023)
source.subject: s0236
source.access: HTTP range extraction of 9 mask members from the 23.5 GB Zenodo zip central directory; the CT image (ct.nii.gz) was NOT downloaded and no image-intensity data is used anywhere in this project
source.label_granularity_note: v2.0.1 labels the jejunum and ileum together as one region `small_bowel` with no lumen; `duodenum` is a separate label (verified against the release member list). Villi (~0.5-1.6 mm) and circular folds are at or below the 1.5 mm voxel pitch.

criteria: small_bowel label entirely inside the field of view (zero voxels on any of the 6 volume faces)
small_bowel label effectively one connected component (largest component >= 99 % of voxels)
both bowel junctions present: small_bowel touches the duodenum label (duodenojejunal flexure) and the caecal end of the colon label (ileocaecal junction)
envelope volume consistent with a published in-vivo small-intestine length at a published calibre

envelope.volume_consistency_note: envelope volume / cross-section of a 20 mm-calibre tube = the length of bowel this abdomen could hold at perfect packing; compared against the published in-vivo 3-5 m

skeleton.why_not_used_as_the_course: adjacent loops touch, so the envelope skeleton merges them into a single branch: its longest path is only 0.47 m, an order of magnitude short of the published in-vivo small-intestine length. The skeleton therefore measures loop territory, not luminal course.

jejunoileal.lattice_pitch_definition: 2 x p75 of the envelope inscribed radius

duodenum.published_reference: duodenum 20-30 cm (Standring, Gray's Anatomy 42nd ed.); the skeleton of a sharply curved C-loop short-cuts the curve, so the measured value is reported below that range as found

centreline.duodenojejunal_bridge_note: straight segment between the duodenal skeleton tip and the first jejunal lattice node; included in the assembled arc length, so total = duodenum + bridge + jejuno-ileum
centreline.published_in_vivo_reference: 3-5 m in vivo (Hounnou et al., Surg Radiol Anat 2002, found a mean of 6.90 m at autopsy with loss of tone; in-vivo intubation and imaging studies give 3-5 m). Measured value is reported, not tuned.

station_boundaries_mm.boundary_note: the jejunum:ileum = 2:3 split is a textbook proportion, not a measurement: parametric

measured_envelope_inscribed_radius_along.note: the subject's bowel is partly decompressed, so the measured inscribed radius is smaller than the published outer radius used for rendering; both are reported
